thread:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike in DSAR deletion failures after the keystore rotation last night. Some deletions hit KMS decrypt errors and are stuck in the erasure queue. Can infra/security weigh in?

raj_infra: I saw a handful of failed jobs in the erasure-processor logs. Error is `DECRYPT_FAILED: key not found` for a subset of snapshots. Suspect a service account lacked new key access during rotation.

elena_sec: Agree with raj. We rotated the cryptoKey and updated the keystore mapping but apparently we didn't propagate the IAM binding to the `dsar-eraser` SA in eu-west1.

tomas_sre: Quick triage steps I'm doing:
1) listing failed items (small sample)
2) confirming KMS key versions and bindings
3) checking if backups/snapshots still reference old ciphertexts

raj_infra: Sample log snippet:
```
2026-03-21T02:14:22Z eraser-processor [job=erase-345] ERROR: DECRYPT_FAILED: cryptoKeyVersion not found projects/redwood/locations/eu/keyRings/kr-01/cryptoKeys/ks-prod/cryptoKeyVersions/3
```

mina_ops: If we need a short-term unblock, we can grant the `dsar-eraser@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` the `cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` role on the new key for 1 hour while we backfill. But that requires an approved retention-exception or emergency breakglass log for audit.

olivia_legal: Legal needs an audit trail if we touch data for failed erasures. If you do a temporary SA grant, document: who, why, start/end times, and approval ticket. Also confirm no data is exported.

elena_sec: Proposed plan:
- Create a timebound IAM binding for `dsar-eraser` (1h) scoped to decrypt only the new key version.
- Run targeted backfill to re-submit erase jobs for the failed list.
- Record actions in incident ticket and retention-exception stub.
- After backfill, remove binding and rotate key version aliases to canonical v4.

maya: That sounds good. One question: will backfilling re-encrypt or attempt to decrypt older ciphertexts? We need to avoid re-encrypting anything.

raj_infra: Backfill will attempt decrypt -> verify -> mark erased. It won't re-encrypt. If decrypt fails, job fails (what we saw). Granting decrypt rights should let it finish.

privacy-bot: Automated note: DSAR work touching keystore requires "forensic" auditflag set on ticket. Please attach `evidence-proof` artefact after completion.

mina_ops: I'll prepare a retention-exception ticket with these fields: scope (list of snapshot IDs), justification (remediate failed erasures from keystore rotation), duration (1 hour), approver (sec lead + legal), mitigation (no export, live audit log).

olivia_legal: Approve in principle. I'll post the formal sign-off in the ticket once sec lead confirms.

elena_sec: Before we do any permission changes, attach the small sample of affected snapshot IDs here so we can sanity-check. Also capture the exact KMS resource name and the IAM diff.

maya: Pasting sample IDs: snapshot-20260318-9a3c, snapshot-20260319-1f7d, snapshot-20260320-ebb2. KMS resource: projects/redwood/locations/eu/keyRings/kr-01/cryptoKeys/ks-prod. Current alias -> v4.

raj_infra: I'll prepare the IAM change and the backfill script. Quick snippet for granting decrypt (one-off):
```
# grant decrypt for exactly 1 hour
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding ks-prod \
  --location=eu --keyring=kr-01 \
  --member=serviceAccount:dsar-eraser@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
# then schedule removal via at + revoke script
```

mina_ops: Note for the retention-exception ticket template: include a field "audit_artifact" with a link to the logs + signed approval. I'll create ticket REQ-20260321-01.

elena_sec: I will validate the IAM binding window and review the logs during the window. If we see any signs of export attempts, we abort and revert.

tomas_sre: I'll throttle backfill to 5 qps to avoid overloading eraser workers.

maya: OK — action owners: raj will apply binding and run backfill, mina will open and own the retention-exception ticket, elena will approve and audit live, olivia will post legal sign-off in the ticket.

raj_infra: Starting to apply changes in 15m. Posting PR and command outputs to the ticket.

mina_ops: Ticket created: REQ-20260321-01 https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/REQ-20260321-01 — added scope and approvers.

olivia_legal: Signed off on ticket subject to sec lead verification.

elena_sec: Verified minimal scope and IAM diff. Approving now.

maya: Thanks all — please keep notes in the ticket. Marking this thread resolved for now, reopen if decrypt errors persist after backfill. :thumbsup:
